verdict.rationale: React renders components into real browser DOM nodes via createRoot and hydrateRoot, and it documents React Developer Tools for inspecting components, editing props and state, and finding performance problems. Together these cover the core of debugging the UI in the browser. Community notes that React manages updates through its own DOM abstraction layer, but it still emits real DOM. Missing for 10: explicit docs that rendered output is inspectable as ordinary elements in native browser devtools (the evidence names React Developer Tools but says little about its browser-devtools integration), and independent hands-on corroboration of the devtools debugging workflow.
